question.leadin: Identify these politicians who were powerful during the 1990's.
question.text: This Georgia Republican served as Speaker of the House from 1995 to 1999 and was a co-writer of the Contract with America.
question.clue: This former Speaker of the House from Georgia won the South Carolina primary. During the campaign, he proposed a moon colony that could petition to become a U.S. state.

swap.text: In a tweet, this South Carolina senator stated that "any policy proposal which drives up costs of Corona, tequila, or margaritas is a big-time bad idea" in response to a 20% income tax with Mexico to pay the wall.
swap.clue: This Senator, who is widely rumored to be gay, has remained low in the polls but was widely regarded as the winner of the September 16th "kid's table" debate.

question.text: This man served as Governor of Florida from 1999-2007, becoming the first two-term Republican governor in the state's history. He is the son of a former US President and the brother of another.
question.clue: Alex Sink, the Democrat defeated by Scott, now makes a historically unique household with her husband Bill McBride, who lost the 2002 Florida Gubernatorial election to this mentor of Marco Rubio.

swap.leadin: In 2010, he resigned as the U.S. Commander in Afghanistan in response to fallout from an interview with Rolling Stone magazine.
swap.text: Name this retired U.S. Army General who criticized Joe Biden and Richard Holbrooke in that article. He previously led the Joint Special Operations Command.
swap.clue: In 2010, Petraeus replaced this commander of American forces in Afghanistan, who resigned following criticism of remarks he made that had been published in Rolling Stone magazine.

question.leadin: Name some Democrats who will undoubtedly be squabbling onstage for the 2016 presidential nomination.
question.text: All signs point to this ex-Secretary of State and rival to Barack Obama in 2008 running, and winning the nomination.
question.clue: This politician's tearful speech at a campaign stop contributed to a comeback win in the 2008 New Hampshire primary.

swap.text: Dan Savage started an Internet movement after this Republican presidential candidate, a Senator from Pennsylvania, made the comment that gay marriage was equal to bestiality in 2003.
swap.clue: This politician was defeated by Bob Casey Jr. in one election.

question.text: This Democratic Party stalwart and Mayor of Chicago from 1955 to 1976 was an alleged racist and was accused of corruption several times.

swap.leadin: She joked that Curt Schilling was a Yankees fan, and Jon Stewart has multiple asthma attacks in a response to this woman losing a certain election.
swap.text: Identify this politician notable for losing a Senate seat election to Scott Brown despite being the Democratic candidate.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the sitting United States Supreme Court.
question.text: This former Rehnquist clerk heard Hamdan v. Rumsfeld once while serving on the DC Circuit Courts, and again while serving as the sitting Chief Justice.
question.clue: In one opinion, this Justice argued that an "individual mandate" should be seen as a tax, and is therefore constitutional.

swap.leadin: He was attacked for being a member of the Concerned Alumni of Princeton, which was accused of being a racist organization.
swap.text: Name this man, who worked as a professor at Seton Hall while serving as a judge on the Third Circuit Court of Appeals.
swap.clue: This justice, the only dissenter in Snyder v. Phelps, was appointed to the Supreme Court in 2005 after the retirement of Sandra Day O'Connor.

question.text: No candidate won a majority in the 1992 election largely because this Texas billionaire received nineteen percent of the popular vote.
question.clue: This Texas businessman who received 18.9% of the popular vote but no electoral votes in a certain election.

swap.text: The sons of one of the founding John Birch Society members are these two brothers, who run a Kansas based conglomerate. They give lots of money to libertarian and conservative groups - particular, they were major donors to Scott Walker's campaign in Wisconsin.

question.text: The CEO of Hewlett-Packard, at the time, was this woman who would go on to unsuccessfully challenge Barbara Boxer in a 2010 senate race.
question.clue: This former CEO of HP and previous candidate for the Republican presidential nomination ran in 2010 for one of California's Senate seats and, in an open-mic gaffe, criticized the haircut of the Democratic opposition, Barbara Boxer.

swap.leadin: Identify the following now-former members of George W. Bush's staff following their recent resignations.
swap.text: This man succeeded Scott McClellan as the third White House press secretary for George W. Bush. He was accused of insulting the press's intelligence when using the word "nuance" to talk about the commutation of Scooter Libby.

question.leadin: Name some members of the cabinet of George W Bush.
question.text: This Taiwan-born politician was the first Chinese American to be appointed to a President's Cabinet, serving as Secretary of Labour for the entire Bush Administration.
question.clue: This 1975 alumna in economics became the first Asian-American woman appointed to a Cabinet position, namely Secretary of Labor by George W. Bush.

swap.leadin: This legislation created the FBI's NICS background check system.
swap.text: Name this bill signed into law by Bill Clinton. It was named in honor of Ronald Reagan's press secretary who took a bullet during John Hinckley's attempted assassination of the president.
swap.answerHtml: Brady Bill [or Brady Act; or Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act]

question.text: The prosecution in the Clinton impeachment was led by this powerful Illinois Republican, the Chairman of the House Judiciary Committee. During the trial, it was revealed that this man had an extramarital affair of his own during the 1960's.

swap.text: The early 1980s also saw this union of air traffic controllers go on strike. Ronald Reagan fired over 11,000 of its members after they refused to return to work.

After she refused to snitch as a star witness in front of the Kefauver committee, she punched several reporters on her way out, exclaiming "I hope an atom bomb falls on all of you!"
